subject: Pilot volume bands, unit economics & credit bridge proposal
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Susan Jones <susan.jones@fastretail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-21T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot volume bands, unit economics & credit bridge proposal

Hi Susan — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and next steps from our discovery/demo:

What we heard
- Primary POC goal: integrate Redwood for customer support generative summarization + response suggestion for 3 EU/US regions.
- Expected pilot traffic (week 1 steady state): 1.2M tokens/day increasing to ~4.5M tokens/day by end of month if NLU routing is enabled.
- Key constraints: 200ms token latency target for suggestions; audit logging and SOC2 evidence required.

Unit-economics framing (proposal)
- We typically price by volume band; our target reference for sizing the pilot: $750 / 1M tokens at the baseline config (fp16) with caching and 8k context.
- Suggested volume bands (pilot):
  * Band A: 0–30M tokens/month -> $1,000 / 1M tokens
  * Band B: 31–120M tokens/month -> $800 / 1M tokens
  * Band C: 121M+ tokens/month -> $600 / 1M tokens
- With your estimate (peaking ~135M tokens/month) you’d land mostly in Band C once warmed up; pilot effective blended target: ~$700–750 / 1M tokens depending on latency profile and caching.

Credits & extension ask
- You mentioned needing additional runway to validate the routing/caching gains; we can offer a one-time credit bridge to cover the early ramp. Details below are a proposed structure we can approve quickly if you confirm the budget band:
  * $15,000 credit applied to usage during a 30-day extension (covers ~20M tokens at baseline price).
  * Guardrails: credit only applies to pilot traffic (tagged API keys); usage above 150M tokens/month will require pre-approval.

Next steps (please confirm)
1) Can you confirm an acceptable target $/1M tokens range for procurement (e.g., $600–$800)?
2) Share whether the pilot will use the 8k or 32k context model (impacts cost).
3) If you want the credit, confirm the internal approver so we can push the small approval through.

Attachments: pilot-volume-bands.xlsx (xlsx, 48 KB); demo recording link above.

Thanks — I’ll loop Ben for approval once you confirm the range.

Connor O'Brien

From: Susan Jones <susan.jones@fastretail.com>

Date: 2026-08-22T09:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot volume bands, unit economics & credit bridge proposal

Thanks Connor — appreciate the clear bands and the demo. A few clarifications: 

- Budget: procurement gave us a soft target of $600–$800 / 1M tokens depending on whether we can hit the 200ms median latency. If you can hit ~200ms with the 8k model we can push toward $600; otherwise expectation is closer to $750.
- Context window: we want to try 8k first and then expand to 32k for long threads in week 3 if the economics look good.
- Credit: the team would value a credit that covers the ramp period. $15k sounds reasonable as a starting point — will need a short note from Redwood indicating it’s a one-time pilot credit applied to tagged API keys.

Next: I can route the approval internally once you provide the credit note (short bullet doc). Also loop in security for SOC2 evidence — they’ll want the auditor checklist.

—Susan
Head of Conversational AI | FastRetail Inc.
[s] susan.jones@fastretail.com
